title: What is known about 1RB1RD_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1RA0LE_1LF0LC_---1LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RD_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1RA0LE_1LF0LC_---1LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a list of counters, runs of the word 011 separated by short words. The last few counters, at the right end, trade amounts with each other and with a block that grows at the end; the older counters to the left are left almost unchanged. The transfer rule is not written down yet. An exact run-length simulation finds no halt in 1015 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 102,439 cells have been visited and 61,465 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: A frozen left part
claims.text: The counters 450, 259, 303, 1011, 731, 2347, 2123 and twenty copies of (011)^11 (110)^11 are the same at steps 10<sup>8</sup> and 2·10<sup>8</sup>.

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>15</sup> steps
claims.text: An exact run-length simulator (c/tok.c; it agrees with tools/c/tmrun.c on the number of 1s at step 10,000,087,134) runs 1015 steps, 2.8·107 visits of the right end in state A, without a halt. The last counters then are 0112482146, 0111085286, 0114382435, 01113188604 and the end block 110495835.

claims.title: No halt in the first 6.64×10<sup>18</sup> steps (exact macro run)
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 6 cells, long runs of equal blocks crossed in one go; exact: every macro step is a run of the machine, counted step for step) ran from blank tape to step 6,645,949,135,344,911,319 without a halt. At this block size it gives the same state, head position and tape as the direct simulator after 2,000,031,220 steps. This is a bounded run and says nothing about later steps.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.603).

claims.title: Active counters at the right end
claims.text: The list keeps about 50–77 tokens; at each moment one of the last counters shrinks at a steady rate (about 1,500 per 10<sup>6</sup> visits) while the end block grows; the first counters (011<sup>410</sup>, 011<sup>255</sup>, ... at 10<sup>6</sup> visits) barely change.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The halting transition F0 is reached as D1 → 0LE, E0 → 1LF; a closed tape language from windows of 4 cells does not confine it to an edge, and the transfer rule of the counters is not known.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0LC_1LC0RE_1LD1LB_1LA1LD_1RF0RA_---1RE up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine keeps a list of counters built from three-cell words; some of them stay frozen in a long regular stretch while others change. This page runs the real machine in your browser.

facts.text: No halt in an exact run-length simulation.
Length of the counter list, steady while the counters grow to millions.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Counters of three-cell words
html: At step 108 the tape reads (111011011)2 (011)450 (110)259 14 (011)303 (110)1011 14 (011)731 (110)2347 14 (011)2123 [14 (011)11 (110)11] × 20 … (101)342 13 (011)420 0 (101)175 …: a list of counters. The left counters (450, 259, 303, ...) were the same at step 2·108; the changes happen at the right end, where new counters appear.

sections.heading: A list of counters
html: Compress the tape into tokens, where 011^c means the word 011 written c times. At every visit of the right end the tape is a list of such counters, separated by short words (0 1111 or 0101 1), with a growing block 110^m at the end:

Only the last few counters are worked on: one of them shrinks at a steady rate while the end block grows, and when it runs out the next one takes over. The first counters of the list change only rarely. The list stays at about 60 tokens while the counters grow to millions, so the machine behaves like a counter machine with a handful of active registers. Their exact transfer rule is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: D on a 1 after two 0s
html: The machine stops only when F reads a 0, reached only as D1 → 0LE, E0 → 1LF: D on a 1 with 0 0 to its left. Inside a run of one word there are never two 0s side by side; they occur only at a few junctions (a separator 0, or 110 next to 011), so a halt needs D to arrive at such a junction in the right way.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: counter list with active counters at the right end
summary: A list of counters 011^c separated by short words; the last few, at the growing right end, are worked on (one shrinks at a steady rate while the end block grows) and the older ones are left behind almost unchanged; no halt in 10^15 steps of an exact run-length simulation.
